questions.title: Amino acid with no chiral centre (2023 printing)
questions.question: Which of the following amino acids is considered optically inactive because it lacks a chiral center?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Valine's alpha carbon carries a branched side chain along with an amino group, a carboxyl group and a hydrogen — four different groups — so it is chiral and optically active.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Alanine's alpha carbon carries a methyl side chain plus the amino group, carboxyl group and hydrogen, again four distinct substituents, so it too has a chiral centre.
explanations.C: Correct. Glycine's side chain is a single hydrogen atom, so its alpha carbon is bonded to two identical hydrogen atoms along with the amino and carboxyl groups — only three distinct groups, not four. This makes glycine the one amino acid with no chiral centre, and therefore the only one that is optically inactive.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Leucine has a bulky branched side chain distinct from the other three groups on its alpha carbon, giving it a chiral centre like the other eighteen standard amino acids besides glycine.

questions.learning_objective: Name glycine as the one amino acid with no chiral centre and therefore no D/L form.
